To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diffusion coefficient and drift mobility in AlGaAs/InGaAs/GaAlAs heterostructures are strongly affected by the electron temperature.
the length coefficient of AlGaAs/GaN is strongly affected by the electric field and that the diffusion coefficient is strongly affected by carrier degeneracy.
the length coefficient shows a maximum at an electric field of 4 kV/cm and the diffusion coefficient is found be strongly affected by carrier degeneracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the non-equilibrium transport of two-dimensional electrons in AlGaAS/GaAs.
the development of a Monte Carlo simulator to calculate the transport properties of hot electrons in two-dimensional electron gas.
the development of a model to predict the performance of AlGaAs/GasAs HBTs, which is based on the Monte Carlo technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diffusion coefficient and the length coefficient are strongly dependent on the degree of degeneracy.
the drift velocity and the diffusion coefficient are not sufficient to describe hot-electron transport in semicondutors.
the drift-diffusion equation is not valid for the transport of hot electrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the drift velocity of the electron gas is determined by the scattering rate of the electrons by the longitudinal-optical phonons.
the diffusion coefficient increases with the electric field, and that the diffusion length decreases with the electric field.
the drift velocity, the diffusion coefficient and the length coefficient are all strongly dependent upon the electric field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the length coefficient is a useful parameter to describe the non-equilibrium transport of electrons.
the diffusion length is not a constant, but varies with the electric field.
the length coefficient is an important transport parameter in addition to diffusion coefficient.
